title: Feature + sprint / execution paths
subtitle: Follow the split at approval, the join at task execution, and the split again when control returns to the caller.

nodes.title: /feature or /sprint
nodes.body:
Resolve same-slug artifacts
Mixed / duplicate matches: STOP
Exact pair or lone spec keeps format

nodes.title: Resume checkpoint
nodes.body:
Draft → approval
Approved spec → planning
Remaining tasks → execution
All accepted → current-proof gate

nodes.title: brainstorming
nodes.body:
Recorded intent + user criteria
Unknowns → open-questions
No guessed product decisions

nodes.title: writing-plans
nodes.body:
Exact criterion IDs → tasks
Paths • tests • dependencies
Checkpoints • prerequisites

nodes.title: Approval is observed
nodes.body:
Feature: sequential spec → plan
Sprint: one initial pair reply
No execution from draft previews
nodes.detail: Only actual host-observed approval over the current armed identity confers the corresponding authority. Pi 1.0.2 has the runtime input seam but codeArbiter has no implemented Pi-native producer; typed admission remains blocked. For prerequisites, show the packet digest and the shared 24-hour request/reply deadline. Cancellation does not create approval.

nodes.title: Small /feature branch
nodes.body: All small-lane conditions → confirm inline criteria → log triage → direct TDD. No spec artifact.

nodes.title: Installed admission is required
nodes.body: Pi HTML admission unavailable; legacy Markdown and inline small lane stay distinct. HTML farm remains blocked.

nodes.title: executing-plans / attended
nodes.body:
/feature: authored HTML checkpoints or bounded legacy batches
Pass selected task IDs; wait for the user between batches

nodes.title: SPRINT.md / approved autonomy
nodes.body:
/sprint: pass the full plan; no attended batch pauses
SMARTS logs choices; delegated methods cannot widen scope

nodes.title: subagent-driven-development
nodes.body:
Resolve current identities → eligible tasks only
HTML: complete contextual read ticket → task-start
Then separately compose and deliver each actor’s scoped input
Legacy Markdown keeps its own dependency/state rules

nodes.title: Fresh scoped author input
nodes.body:
Map + commands + constraints
Native instructions; actual actor delivery
No inherited prior-task narrative

nodes.title: tdd / six gates
nodes.body:
1 Obligations → 2 Red → 3 Green
4 Obligation verify → 5 Coverage → 6 Lint
Missing proof loops back to the failing gate
Coverage-auditor where contract/security critical

nodes.title: Spec-compliance review
nodes.body:
Fresh independent reviewer input
Exact task obligation + current source
Failure → corrective author brief
nodes.detail: Independent task-spec review and actual source-bound observations still precede acceptance. The current source repairs Claude launch/child correlation and native Unicode observation hashing; neither repair substitutes an author’s report for a reviewer receipt. Re-arm requests made stale by the applicable engine upgrade rather than relabeling old evidence.

nodes.title: Fresh task verification
nodes.body:
Run the plan’s proving command again
Read output and exit code
HTML: real producer-owned receipts

nodes.title: Task proof / provisional review
nodes.body: HTML task-review binds spec-review + verification receipts. REVIEW is not ACCEPTED.

nodes.title: Next eligible task in the same scope
nodes.body: Repeat fresh author → spec proof → fresh verification. No context accumulation across task authors.

nodes.title: Correction is not permission to waive a gate
nodes.body:
Approved sprint: diagnose, reconcile, retry with fresh proof.
Same failure twice without new evidence: stop that strategy.
Authority / security / CONFIRM gaps still stop affected work.
nodes.detail: After interruption, resume through the existing exact identity and durable operation outcome. Correct stale context or missing authority at its own boundary. The newer engine wait defaults to 120 seconds, but this is not a latency objective or an extension of outer host deadlines. This atlas does not benchmark runtime responsiveness.

nodes.title: Combined quality review
nodes.body:
Once per authored scope / checkpoint
Actual combined diff + fresh reviewer inputs
No CRITICAL/HIGH; rerun after corrections
Scope of one uses the same rule

nodes.title: accept-scope / current proof
nodes.body:
HTML: one whole-scope operation
All required current receipts must agree
Markdown: authoritative ledger transition
No rendered labels as authority

nodes.title: Attended return
nodes.body:
Batch complete → executing-plans
User checkpoint before next batch

nodes.title: Full plan complete
nodes.body:
Current acceptance preflight
Commit owner retains permission gate

nodes.title: Authorized delivery
nodes.body:
commit-gate → finishing owner
Sprint: open PR only
Feature: selected terminal disposition
No automatic merge

edges.label: record task proof, not final acceptance
all tasks in current scope have spec proof + fresh verification

panels.title: 01  /  SELECT AUTHORITY BEFORE EXECUTION
panels.caption: An existing pipeline resumes from its exact format. New full-lane work defaults to HTML, never a silent Markdown fallback.

panels.title: 02  /  CHOOSE THE COORDINATOR
panels.caption: The approved caller, not the author agent, controls scope and pacing.

panels.title: 03  /  ONE TASK, ONE FRESH AUTHOR CONTEXT
panels.caption: The actual order is per-task spec review + fresh verification, then combined quality once the current scope is ready.

panels.title: 04  /  COMBINED-SCOPE ACCEPTANCE AND CALLER RETURN
panels.caption: Per-task progress cannot bypass this barrier. Direct fix/refactor and small-feature lanes keep their own TDD close.

notes.text: Optional branches: using-git-worktrees isolates opted-in units; legacy --farm replaces authoring, never review. Neither is the default.
Reselect actor context after resume, compaction or worktree/scope change. An engine ticket or parent persona marker is not a child delivery receipt.
